As a developer, I want endpoints to be able to return raw bytes so that binary or pre-encoded responses can be sent unchanged.
As an API client, I want JSON endpoints to return JSON-serializable Python dicts or lists (or use jsonify) so that I can parse responses as JSON reliably.
As a developer, I want responses declared with a TypedDict to include the required keys (for example, a 'status' key) so that consumers can rely on a stable response structure.
As an API client, I want endpoints implemented with generators or iterators to stream data incrementally so that large sequences can be consumed without loading everything into memory.
As a tester, I want the /status/<int:code> endpoint to accept an integer parameter and return the body with that integer as the HTTP status code so that different status responses can be exercised.
As a developer, I want endpoints to be able to return an HTTPStatus enum value as the status in a response tuple so that semantic HTTP status names can be used instead of raw integers.
As a developer, I want each route path to be uniquely registered (no duplicate route definitions) so that routing behavior is deterministic and one handler does not unintentionally override another.

As a developer, I want view functions' actual responses to match their declared return types (str, bytes, Response, dict, list, generator, iterator, tuple, TypedDict) so that type checking and runtime behavior remain consistent and predictable.
